name: JingYu Sun
about: I am a master's student in Software Engineering at Northwestern Polytechnical University. My research interests lie in embodied intelligence and multimodal learning, with a focus on vision-language-action models and selective video-to-audio generation.

I am currently researching embodied intelligence as an intern at the State Grid AI Laboratory. I am also interested in world models and the adaptation of large language models to practical applications.

projects.title: Robot-state understanding and error correction
projects.label: Ongoing research
projects.description: Exploring error correction for robotic manipulation on top of MemoryVLA. Using Qwen3-VL to automate annotations of Bridge subtask data and train a model to recognize robot states.

projects.title: A retrieval-augmented legal assistant
projects.label: Applied language models
projects.description: Built a domain-specific assistant around Qwen2.5-7B, combining QLoRA instruction tuning, DPO preference alignment, and two-stage retrieval with BGE embeddings and reranking. A Gradio interface supports streaming conversations and displays the relevant legal sources.

research.title: Seeing What Matters for Action: Bridging Visual Priors and Robotic Control in Vision-Language-Action Models
research.summary: Visual foundation models offer rich perceptual knowledge, but not every visual detail helps a robot choose the right action. ActSight combines action-sensitive visual refinement with temporal representation alignment, preserving control-relevant cues and relationships across neighboring observations. Across manipulation tasks, it improves control performance over direct feature alignment and visual-enhancement baselines.

research.title: Beyond Target Matching: Measuring and Mitigating Non-Target Leakage in Selective Video-to-Audio Generation
research.summary: Generating the requested sound is only part of selective video-to-audio generation: other visible sources should remain silent. FocusV2A uses a target prompt to select relevant visual evidence before generating audio, while VGG-SourcePair evaluates both target retention and non-target leakage in dual-source scenes. Experiments show stronger source selectivity while maintaining competitive audio quality and audiovisual synchronization.
